name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing computer or program using software, system, or service bugs including SQL injection, server-side template injection, and command injection.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript (XSS)
description: Adversaries may execute malicious JavaScript in web browser sessions using Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) to capture user cookies, tokens, or redirect browsing sessions.

name: Data from Local System: Path Traversal / LFI
description: Adversaries may search local system files and directory trees using directory traversal (../, ..\) to locate sensitive configuration files, password hashes (/etc/passwd, win.ini), and source code.

name: Brute Force: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries may systematically guess passwords against authentication gateways or brute-force user accounts to gain unauthorized credential access.

name: Active Scanning: Vulnerability & Wordlist Probing
description: Adversaries may actively scan web applications with wordlists (dirbuster, ffuf, gobuster) to discover exposed administration portals, configuration decoys, and debug routes.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Adversaries may attempt to make payloads difficult to discover or analyze using Base64, hex encoding, URL double-encoding, comment interleaving, and case manipulation.

name: File and Directory Discovery: Canary Trap Hits
description: Adversaries probe hidden paths (.env, backup.sql, .git/config, wp-login.php) seeking credentials or backup data, triggering decoy honeypot tripwires.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol / C2
description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating files or database dumps to an external command-and-control server or web endpoint.
